text:
Kevin Fiala returned to the Kings lineup on November 12 and has played six games since, all at around 16 minutes a night. He has two assists and no goals on seven shots, and the early five-on-five picture is rough: Los Angeles has had 38.5% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, with him on the ice, 11.86 points below its rate without him. Six games after a long absence is a tiny sample, and it reads like a player getting his legs back.

The talent hasn't gone anywhere. His top shot this season clocks in the 93rd percentile on NHL EDGE, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.0 scoring chances per 60 from the slot last season, 89th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey's verdict on 2025-26 was harsh on the results (about replacement level) but kinder on the process: 1.1 expected wins built from his chances. Our numbers project 38 points. Watch whether the shot volume comes back first; the goals usually follow it.
headline: Fiala is back and still waiting for a goal
